item.content:encoded:
I believe that, as writers, incorporating methods that force us to reconsider our usual well-trod trends for placing certain words next to one another is imperative for revolutionary discovery. Doing so can produce nonsensical gibberish but also compositional gems that might never have been discovered within the confines of unassisted human thinking — both of which are featured here.

Personally, I came across phrases and pairings of words in this that floored me.

+ show block
– hide block

hissing sounds of blackened laughter

and

Someone who I’ve tasted countless miles of

Belong in good poetry.

Light wrinkled over the cloud edge

Gorgeous and novel.

murdered communion

pointing at someone with enough brains to get laid

upon this handsome world of trouble.

“But what value does decades of research have if my balls throb with deafening rage?”

lol oh my lord. Write a better sentence, I dare you.

049 was high rated prior to the rewrite but we still believed that it was low enough below our current standards that it deserved a rewrite.

No, it was rewritten because the original author decided to rewrite it. That is the only reason it was rewritten.

Ratings don't determine quality, they determine survivability.

This is correct. Articles don't "belong" or "not-belong" on the site (as you previously put it); they persist on the merit of how many upvotes vs downvotes they have. If you think an article doesn't belong here, you down-vote it. You may also state why you voted the way you voted, though you should be polite — and refrain from hyperbole or insulting rhetoric.

Now that we've clarified this, I presume we can move on.

item.content:encoded:
Another article like this is just lowering the standards for articles created here

The only objectively measurable 'standard' for content on this site being 'good' or not is an article's rating. Maybe this article will end up low-rated and overlooked, but what consequence is there if it does? Its URL is /pounded… did any other type of article need that URL? And maybe it'll make a lot of people laugh and end up high-rated. Either way, does the source really matter if the content is still upvote-worthy (in some people's opinion)?

Edit: I suppose I also should have put "good" in quotation marks. What I meant is that an upvote represents one person saying "I want this here and like it". It is a system that relies on the majority's opinion, for better or worse. (That does not mean articles can't get old and have not-statistically-provable community 'standards' change; that wasn't even what this topic was about as far as I'm aware. If something's upvoted, it's here, that's all there is to it.)

item.title: boy oh boy
item.content:encoded:
So here we are again. I didn't want to just do another SCP-\̅\̅\̅\̅-J, so I held off on doing any more Botnik-generated articles until I had a solid idea of how to make the next one unique in its own right. Then I found out that there was an existing Chuck Tingle Botnik keyboard, and the rest was history.

Please note that Botnik is simply a tool, and there is a large human component to the writing process. I know that some folks would probably prefer Botnik to have been a one-and-done thing, but, eh. I had fun writing this and I wanted to share it.

Special thanks to anqxyr for the SCP Ebooks that made this possible!

Make your own erotic masterpiece here!
